newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen up on Thursdsay.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen up on Thursdsay.

text.p: Polish shares eased for the third straight session, but analysts said the market should rebound on Thursday, powered by stronger buying after price fixing and rises in continuous trade, which ends later.
Some analysts said, however, that it was possible the market's month-long horizontal trend would continue amid a general lack of positive signals to help spur growth.

"No one doubts there'll be growth tomorrow, the question is whether after the growth there'll be stronger selling after price fixing with people closing positions,", said Pawel Hominski, an analyst at Magnus brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.3 percent to 13,531.0 and turnover fell 9.5 percent to 77.4 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts said a good signal was a rise in active trade by large-cap stocks such as top gainers Kety, Exbud and BIG, up 2.5, 1.3 and 1.3 percent.
They said this reflected buying by large investors which could soon help form a growth trend.
But they also said Kety's rise was in part a reaction to an exaggerated low-turnover fall on Tuesday and that some large-cap stocks have fallen of late as well.

"They (large investors) are buying and selling -- there's an exchange going on and there doesn't seem to be such a preponderance of buying," said Waldemar Gebus, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital & Investment.
Continuous trade turnover was 3.4 million zlotys with five stocks up and three flat.
NFI units eased 0.7 percent to 139.5 zlotys in a 13.2-million-zloty turnover but rose 2.6 percent to 140.5 zlotys in 14.5-million-zloty continuous trade.
